seo_title: Menu bar pomodoro timer for macOS
seo_description: PomodoroPace is a free, open-source menu bar pomodoro timer for macOS. Task labels, daily session counts, a seven-day chart and a gentle chime.
hero_sub: A native pomodoro timer with task labels, daily session counts and a gentle chime when each block ends. Open the popover, then press Space to start.
features_sub: Three phases, honest history and quiet alerts, with nothing leaving your Mac.

features.title: Focus, short and long breaks
features.desc: Defaults to 25, 5 and 15 minutes, with a long break after a block count you choose. Auto-start the next break or focus block if you like.

features.title: Label every block
features.desc: Add an optional task label to each focus block and pick from your 50 most recent labels.

features.title: Daily and weekly history
features.desc: See today's completed blocks, daily and weekly counts with total focused minutes, and a seven-day bar chart.

features.title: A chime when time is up
features.desc: Choose from 14 built-in macOS sounds with a preview button, plus a notification. If notifications are denied, the menu bar title flashes instead.

features.title: Keyboard-first controls
features.desc: In the popover, Space starts or pauses, S skips and R resets. The shortcuts are ignored while you type a label.

features.title: Survives sleep and clock changes
features.desc: Blocks track a monotonic deadline, so time zone and clock changes do not break them. A setting decides whether time asleep counts toward the block.

permissions_step: When prompted, allow notifications for PomodoroPace (System Settings > Notifications) so you see a banner when a block ends; Login Items is only needed if you enable Launch at login.

faq.q: Is PomodoroPace really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license, the full source is on GitHub, and there are no ads, accounts or in-app purchases. If you find it useful, there is an optional Support button in the app.

Notifications, requested at first launch to show a banner when a block ends. Login Items is used only if you turn on Launch at login. It does not ask for Accessibility, Screen Recording, Microphone or any other privacy permission.

Only on your Mac. Settings and recent labels live in UserDefaults, and session history is a JSON file at ~/Library/Application Support/PomodoroPace/history.json. History older than a year is pruned, and the app makes no network calls.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, and this is a free project. Right-click the app and choose Open once to get past Gatekeeper, or build it yourself from source with Xcode.
